newsitem.title: UK: Queens Moat eyes sale of Bath luxury hotel.
newsitem.headline: Queens Moat eyes sale of Bath luxury hotel.

text.p: Luxury hotel group Cliveden Plc said it was in talks to buy the prestigious Royal Crescent Hotel in Bath, south west England, from Queens Moat Houses Plc.
It said no formal agreement had been entered into and a further announcement would be made "as and when appropriate."
Cliveden said that if the deal went ahead, funding would come from existing resources. It gave no financial details.
The Royal Crescent is a luxury hotel set in Bath's famous Georgian district in a street of the same name.
Queens Moat currently has some 27 hotels up for sale and most, like the Royal Crescent, are in its up-market County portfolio.
The company aims to sell these and focus its business on the mid-market Moathouse chain, of which it has 50-60 hotels.
Queens Moat has said it will use the proceeds from selling the hotels to reduce debt.
It trimmed its pretax, pre-exceptional losses to 2.5 million stg in the year ending December 31, 1995 from a 59.5 million stg loss previously.
Cliveden was floated on the stock exchange in April.

It owns the British stately home of the same name which rose to notoriety in the Cold War as the place where an affair between British War Minister John Profumo and 19-year-old prostitute Christine Keeler began at a weekend party.
Profumo was forced to resign from parliament after lying about his affair with Keeler, who was also sleeping with a Soviet naval attache.
